source.title: Unlocking Multi-Task Electric Energy System Intelligence: Data Scaling Laws and Performance with Limited Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Shao-Huai Liu; Lin Dong; Chao Tian; Le Xie

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or document mismatch. Figure contents are not numerically transcribed in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Extends data-scaling analysis to fine-tuning for power-system tasks and reports scenario-generalization results. It does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports power-system task performance across training-data sizes and parameter sizes. Numerical values for the data-scaling curves and fitted laws are not present in the text; those results are recorded as figure-only. The cited NLP scaling-law results are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama 3 models on power-system QA tasks. It fits power laws of held-out task metrics against fine-tuning data size, which bears on V5's fine-tuning regime. It also compares downstream task metrics across 1B, 3B and 8B models, which bears on V6. It does not measure pretraining loss, so V1–V4 are not tested. V7 is not tested because no fit-dependence or curve-bending analysis is done.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that scenario-generalization task performance scales approximately as a power law with fine-tuning data. They find this holds in multi-task training without interference between tasks, and that satisfactory performance needs relatively little data. Parameter scaling from 1B to 8B gives limited, inconsistent gains, so small models suffice and extreme scaling is unnecessary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning of Llama 3 models on power-system question-answer demonstrations, with scenario-generalization task metrics and log-linear data fits; it does not reproduce language-model pretraining loss scaling experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares single-task, three-task, and six-task training; it reports similar performance across the compared task-training settings. It also reports task-dependent parameter-size results.
record.problems: The experiments use one grid topology (IEEE-118) and primarily synthetic simulation data. Numerical curve values and fitted coefficients are not transcribed in the supplied text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The parameter-size comparison uses only 1B, 3B, and 8B models.

untested.parts: Other modalities, repeated data, and transfer. Power-law fits against model size or compute in fine-tuning. Fine-tuning loss itself (only task metrics are fitted).
Prediction from pretraining loss. Fitted scaling curves or extrapolation across model size; only three sizes are compared.
The authors say the laws could serve as predictive tools but never test extrapolation.

missing.what: Fitted power-law equations and correlation coefficients r for each task's data-scaling curve. These are given in the figure legends but not as text.
Training time per loop grows roughly linearly with parameters (1.12s, 4.37s, 9.96s). This is a compute cost, not a loss result.

record.verdict_notes: The domain is far from language-model pretraining. The metrics are task errors after LoRA fine-tuning on synthetic IEEE-118 data, with no uncertainty estimates. The model-size comparison confounds parameter count with each model's different pretraining. The 1B rows (R13, R16, R19, R22, R25) are reference baselines, not tests. Kaplan et al. is cited only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation as compute changes.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and regimes beyond the study's power-system tasks and supervised fine-tuning.
Downstream-task predictability from pretraining loss; broad prediction across models, tasks, or scales.
Whether exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on fitting choices, or whether curves bend away from power laws.

relationships.condition: LoRA fine-tuning of Llama 3 on six IEEE-118 power-system tasks, single-task and multi-task
relationships.reason: The authors report that log-log fits of task metrics against fine-tuning data size are approximately power-law across all tasks and training mixes (R1–R12). The evidence is figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Task metrics show approximately power-law dependence on fine-tuning data across all six tasks and single-task and multi-task training mixes.

relationships.condition: OPF optimality gap and transient prediction MSE across 1B, 3B and 8B
relationships.reason: Both metrics improve monotonically with parameter count (R14, R15, R20, R21).
relationships.display_finding: Optimality gaps and transient prediction MSE both decreased monotonically across 1B, 3B and 8B models.

relationships.condition: Fault detection error rate and state estimation MSE across 1B, 3B and 8B
relationships.reason: Fault detection is flat at 25% (R17, R18). State estimation MSE is worse at 3B and 8B than at 1B (R26, R27).
relationships.display_finding: Fault detection error stayed at 25%, while state estimation MSE was higher at 3B and 8B than at 1B.

relationships.reason: The trend is non-monotonic: 3B is far worse (0.088, possibly a typo) while 8B is slightly better than 1B (R23, R24).
relationships.display_finding: The 3B model had a much worse reported MSE of 0.088, while 8B performed slightly better than 1B.
